items.summary: An Interpol executive warns AI is making existing cyber threats faster and harder to detect, while companies face new risks from the rise of agentic AI.

items.title: ‘I have $400,000 in equity’: I’m 80. Should I sell my house because of dangerous stairs — or spend thousands renovating?
items.summary: “Generally, the advice I’ve read says not to sell because I have a low-interest-rate mortgage.”
items.zh: “我有 40 万美元的净资产”：我已经 80 岁了。我应该因为楼梯危险而卖掉我的房子，还是花数千美元进行翻修？

items.title: Your voice may reveal how fast you're aging, new AI 'speech clock' suggests
items.summary: A new machine-learning "speech clock" estimates a person's chronological age from their speech, drawing links between older-sounding speech and cognitive decline.
items.zh: 新的人工智能“语音时钟”表明，你的声音可能会揭示你衰老的速度

items.title: Physicists unveil the most accurate atomic clock ever ‪—‬ and it could literally redefine the second
items.summary: Physicists have used radioactive lutetium to create what they say is the most accurate atomic clock ever, keeping time perfectly up to 19 decimal places.
items.zh: 物理学家推出了有史以来最精确的原子钟——它实际上可以重新定义秒

items.title: With most information hidden, the game Stratego had stumped AI—until now
items.summary: Adding in a second neural network that guesses the identity of hidden pieces was key.

items.title: Watch the world's smallest crocodiles snatch bats in their hidden underground lair ‪—‬ a behavior never seen before
items.summary: Live Science can exclusively reveal a video of Gabon's mysterious cave-dwelling dwarf crocodiles snatching bats in a never-before-seen hunting behavior, ahead of the series premiere of "Africa: Earth's Wild Home."
items.zh: 观看世界上最小的鳄鱼在隐藏的地下巢穴中抓走蝙蝠——这是以前从未见过的行为

items.title: Adversity shaped our evolution as a species. People raised in it may have underrecognized strengths because of it.
items.summary: Psychologists have long studied the deficits associated with being raised in adversity. They're now discovering the hidden strengths that can emerge in those settings.
items.zh: 逆境塑造了我们作为一个物种的进化。在这种环境中长大的人可能因此而没有得到充分认识。

items.title: 'This is what happened with Claude and me': AI's failed attempt to crack the Riemann hypothesis led mathematician to a breakthrough

items.title: Here’s how brain-eating amoebas may infect people
items.summary: Naegleria amoebas’ exploration skills and crawling behaviors could help explain how the brain-eating variety travel into human brains.

items.zh: 第四维度实际上是什么样子？

items.title: This new qubit could be 100 times less error-prone in superfluid quantum computer breakthrough
items.summary: A proposed qubit made with superfluid helium could cut quantum computing error rates by around 100 times by shielding quantum information from common forms of electromagnetic noise. If experiments confirm the predictions, the technology could eventually work alongside today’s superconducting qubits
items.zh: 在超流量子计算机突破中，这种新的量子位的出错率可能会降低 100 倍

items.zh: 这种饮食可以延缓大脑衰老 2.5 年

items.title: A video of a humpback whale and her dead calf reveals the animals’ bond
items.summary: A female humpback whale may have spent days with her stillborn calf. This rare sighting may suggest that baleen whales experience grief.
items.zh: 一段关于座头鲸和她死去的小鲸鱼的视频揭示了这些动物之间的联系

items.title: Could quitting ultra-processed food boost your mental health?
items.summary: People with depression who dramatically cut ultra-processed foods experienced notable improvements in their symptoms in a small preliminary study. Researchers suspect healthier eating may benefit the brain partly by reducing gut damage and chronic inflammation.
items.zh: 戒掉超加工食品可以改善您的心理健康吗？

items.title: Alzheimer’s risk gene APOE4 may have a reversible weakness
items.summary: The Alzheimer’s risk gene APOE4 may actively damage brain blood vessels and sabotage the cellular systems that remove harmful proteins. Researchers were able to reverse some of these effects in experiments, revealing promising new targets for Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, and other neurodegenerative dis
items.zh: 阿尔茨海默病风险基因 APOE4 可能存在可逆弱点

items.title: Dinosaur-killing impact crater might have been teeming with life
items.summary: Hot, nutrient water might have lasted for over 5 million years after the impact.

items.title: A local network of implants uses your body as the wiring
